subject: general
question: Which of the following non-biodegradable substances may be inert and simply persist in the environment for a long time or may harm the various members of the eco-system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastic made material**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plastic materials are non-biodegradable, meaning they do not break down naturally in the environment.
 
• They can persist for hundreds to thousands of years, causing long-term pollution.
 
• Plastic waste can harm wildlife, including ingestion by marine and terrestrial animals, leading to injury or death.
 
• Microplastics, small plastic particles, can accumulate in the food chain, posing health risks to humans and animals.
 
• Efforts to manage plastic waste include recycling, reduction in use, and development of biodegradable alternatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodegradable vs Non-biodegradable:**

 
 
• Biodegradable substances are capable of being decomposed by bacteria or other living organisms.
 
• Non-biodegradable substances, like plastics, do not break down naturally and can persist in the environment.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Non-biodegradable waste contributes to pollution, harming ecosystems and biodiversity.
 
• Plastic pollution is a significant environmental issue, affecting oceans, rivers, and terrestrial habitats.
 
 
 
• **Recycling and Management:**
 
 
• Recycling is a key strategy to reduce plastic waste, but not all plastics are recyclable.
 
• Innovations in biodegradable plastics are being developed to reduce environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives:**
 
 
• International agreements, such as the Basel Convention, aim to manage and reduce plastic waste globally.
 
• Countries are implementing bans on single-use plastics to mitigate environmental damage.
